doc.title: Urbie Green interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, Majesty of the Seas, May 29, 1995

title: Freddie Green, microphones and balance in recording
summary: Discusses whether Freddie Green was amplified and how one-microphone recordings gave way to isolated studio tracks.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Making records: studios, takes and the technology

blocks.x: Yeah. I think he might have had a microphone, I’m not even sure. I mean it wasn’t a pick-up, an electric pick-up, it wasn’t that kind of amplification where it’s attached to the
guitar. But I think he probably, well everybody had a microphone in the recording studio, although in the earlier days sometimes they did all those records with one microphone.
That means it had to be balanced.

Like the Carnegie Hall jazz thing that Benny Goodman did I think with just one microphone, so they’d balance themselves. And over the years it’s gotten so everybody is really isolated in the studios now. You’ve got your own microphone and your own earphones and so the whole balance is left to the engineer, whereas getting a balance within yourselves is not all that important anymore or critical.
